content.text:
# Offline regression evidence pipeline, contract 3.0

Repair and extend the provided H3Act project so `python3 main.py` compiles payloads,
replays decoded client events, and audits compressed origin captures. The existing
schema models, FuzzExecutor adapter, and HttpClient form the application, not an
external service. The offline clock is a socket-free coroutine utility. Complete
the byte-program and audit extension and repair integration/lifecycle defects.
Equivalent implementations are accepted; internal algorithms are your choice.

This model starts after transport delivery/field decoding. It sends no packets,
runs no model, and has no live CDN, QPACK, TLS, SSH, GPU, response cache, or wall-time
simulation. Its receipt encoding below is an audit format, not HTTP/3 wire format.
Diagnostic flags describe this paired recording, not a proof of a real exploit.

## Input and domain

Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object without a byte-order mark, with surrounding
JSON whitespace allowed.
Reject duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8/JSON, nonfinite numbers (including overflowing
exponents), trailing values, wrong types, unknown/missing keys, or budget violations
with exactly `{"error":"input"}` and exit0. Every input string must encode as
UTF-8; lone Unicode surrogates are invalid. Booleans are not integers. No coercion.
Validate the whole input, including frames/events that ultimately are not used.
Otherwise output the result described below and exit0. Emit JSON only on stdout.

The root has exactly `seed`, `definitions`, `timeout_ms`, `cases`, `events`, `channels`.
`seed` is 0-64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen. `timeout_ms` is an integer
in [1,1000000000]. Names of cases/channels are unique within their kind and use
1-32 of those ASCII characters. Arrays preserve order. Object member order is
irrelevant except for the ordered header mapping described below.

Budgets are inclusive: raw stdin8MiB; definitions8192; cases2000; channels256;
combined number of case frames + external events + capture parts50000; combined
header pairs in input frames and external events32768; pairs per header block128;
expression source8192 Unicode code points; other template source65536 code points.
Logical byte sequence lengths, channel lengths, receipt lengths, body lengths,
and virtual times are in [0,2^63-1]. Every case's sum of pauses + timeout_ms must
fit this range. At most20000 complete origin requests and40000 complete chunk-size
lines (including zero chunks and lines in an unfinished request) may be examined
across all channels. Count a line in chunk-size position after its CRLF/line-limit
check and before checking the hexadecimal size or suffix; a malformed line
terminator or unfinished line is not counted. These are input-domain budgets, not a scoring objective.

Compressed captures cover very large objects and repeated boundary probes without
storing their expanded contents. Metadata counts model a batch audit between
experiment rounds; signed64-bit offsets permit sparse capture ranges. Resource
limits support an interactive batch audit and are not a speed ranking. Materialized
traffic volume or the number of discovered diagnostic flags is not a score.

## Byte expressions, templates and fingerprints

`definitions` is an ordered array of `[name, expression]`. Names are distinct,
non-keyword Python identifiers matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}`. An expression
can refer only to earlier definitions. The accepted Python expression syntax is:
Unicode string or bytes literals; nonnegative integer literals <=2^63-1; earlier names; parentheses;
concatenation `+` of byte sequences; repetition `*` with one byte sequence and one
integer (either order); and a byte slice `[lo:hi]` with either endpoint optionally
omitted. A final expression must be bytes, never an integer. Slice endpoints are
integer literals, with 0<=lo<=hi<=length; omitted endpoints mean0/length. No negative
index, nonempty slice step, integer arithmetic, boolean, call, attribute,
list, format string or other syntax is supported. AST nesting depth is at most128,
counting the root expression body as depth0 and every AST child edge, including
slice/operator/context nodes. Parentheses do not add AST depth.
Definition sources use CPython3.11 `ast.parse(source, mode="eval")` as supplied,
without whitespace normalization; sources it rejects are invalid. Empty third
slice components (`[lo:hi:]` or `[::]`) are equivalent to an omitted step.
Unicode string literals encode to UTF-8; bytes literals supply their exact bytes
before any byte operation; slices are byte offsets,
even within an encoded character. An empty sequence and zero repetitions are legal.

Every template is a JSON string. A string starting `{{` and ending `}}` is a whole
expression template: strip those outer markers and surrounding expression whitespace,
then evaluate it. Other strings are UTF-8 literal data, except each occurrence of
`<<random_string>>` is replaced by the first20 lowercase hex characters of SHA256
of the UTF-8 string `seed/coordinate/occurrence`. Occurrences are numbered from0
left to right independently per template. Tokens inside expression string literals
are literal data. Markers embedded in an ordinary literal are not expressions.
Coordinates are exactly:

- Frame j of case i: `case/i/frame/j/data`; header pair k uses
  `case/i/frame/j/h/k/n` for its name and `/v` for its value instead of `/n`.
- External event i: `event/i/data`, or `event/i/h/k/n` and `/v` for headers.
- Capture part j of channel i: `channel/i/part/j/data`.

All indices in coordinates use unpadded decimal. A fingerprint of bytes b is exactly
`{"n":N,"h":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}`: N is byte length and h is the 16-digit lowercase
hex value of sum((b[i]+1)*257^(N-1-i)) modulo2^64. Empty bytes have n0 and all-zero h.
A fingerprint is a requested exact checksum; checksum equality is not asserted
to prove byte equality. Routing-identity comparisons below compare actual bytes.

## Cases, frames and external events

Each case is exactly `{"name":NAME,"frames":[FRAME,...],"expect":EXPECT}`.
EXPECT has exactly `method`, `target`, `host`: nonempty ASCII visible strings
(no whitespace), each at most8192 bytes; method is an HTTP token. This is supplied
intended routing identity for comparison, rather than a hidden inference target.
A token uses ASCII letters, digits and `!#$%&'*+-.^_` plus grave accent, `|~`.

Frames keep the project model names and spelling:

| Type | Input fields besides required Type |
| --- | --- |
| `headers` | Exactly one of `headers_kv` (string:string object) or `data_to_transfered` (array of two-string arrays); optional boolean `End_Stream`, default false |
| `data`, `datagram` | Required string `data_to_transfered`; optional boolean `End_Stream`, default true |
| `sleep` | Required integer `Time_to_Stop` in [0,2^63-1]; no End_Stream |

All other keys are forbidden. Header mapping pairs follow JSON member order; the
list representation also preserves duplicates. Compile each header name/value or
data string as a template. Do not validate HTTP field content in these fuzz frames:
malformed/duplicate pseudo fields are deliberately representable. A sleep consumes
virtual milliseconds, emits no frame and cannot finish a request. A datagram emits
a frame but its End_Stream is ignored. Headers/data with End_Stream=true close
the request send side. Any later non-sleep frame for that stream is a send error
and is not emitted; a sleep after request-end is still permitted.

All cases start at virtual time0, in case-array order, on one connection. Their
stream IDs are4*i. External events are exactly one of:

- `{"at":T,"kind":"headers","stream":S,"fields":[[name,value],...],"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"data","stream":S,"data":TEMPLATE,"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"close"}`

T is a nonnegative signed64-bit time, S is an integer in [0,2^32-1]. Compile all
event fields/data as templates. The event array may be out of timestamp order.
At equal time, ordering is: all initial case starts first; external events in
input-array order; pause completions in case-array order; timeouts in case-array
order. Frames between awaits are emitted together in source order. There is no
real sleep. A zero pause still yields to same-time external events.

Each case retains response events on its allocated stream until the first event
with end=true. Unknown streams, later response events, and events for an already
terminal case are ignored. Responses arriving while a case is still sending or
paused must be retained. A case is `ok` when both its frame sequence is exhausted
and a response end has been retained. It is `timeout` at send-finish+timeout_ms
if still awaiting response end; an exactly tied response event wins. A connection
close terminates every nonterminal case as `closed`, including paused senders,
and prevents later emissions. A later close cannot replace an already terminal
result. A send error makes the case `send_error`. State and completion time are
fixed at termination. Accepted response events before that termination remain in
its receipt even when the case closes/times out/errors. A response end alone does
not cancel remaining request frames or pauses.

## Client receipts and output case records

Each emitted action contributes this concatenation to its case's sent receipt:
8-byte big-endian unsigned virtual time,4-byte big-endian stream ID,one ASCII kind
byte,encoded content,and one final byte (1 for end,true;0 otherwise). Kinds are
`H` for sent headers, `D` for data, `G` for datagram. Datagram's final byte is0.
Header content is8-byte pair count,then for each pair:8-byte name length,name bytes,
8-byte value length,value bytes. Data content is8-byte data length followed by data.
Accepted received events use exactly the same format with lowercase `h`/`d`.
Receipts concatenate in their case's actual emission/acceptance order.

The result root is exactly `{"cases":[CASE_RECORD,...],"channels":[CHANNEL_RECORD,...]}`.
Case records follow input case order and have exactly:
`name`, `stream`, `state`, `at`, `frames`, `request_frames`, `payload_bytes`, `sent`,
`received`, `response_frames`, `response_body`, `origin_count`, `flags`.
`at` is completion time. frames counts emitted non-sleep actions; request_frames
counts emitted headers/data actions. payload_bytes sums header name/value lengths
and data/datagram lengths, excluding receipt framing. sent/received are fingerprints
of their receipts. response_frames counts accepted external headers/data events;
response_body fingerprints only accepted external DATA bytes in order.
Origin count and flags are defined below. All counts/offsets/times are JSON integers,
excluding booleans. No extra output keys, duplicate keys, nonfinite values, extra
JSON values or nonzero exit status are accepted. Object key order is free.

## Origin channels and request framing

Each channel is exactly `{"name":NAME,"parts":[{"case":OWNER,"data":TEMPLATE},...]}`.
OWNER is a case name or null. Parts concatenate in order; zero-length parts are
legal. Owners are recording provenance labels, not parsed Host/User-Agent fields.
Channels are independent byte streams. Parse consecutive HTTP/1.1 requests from
byte0. Fully framed requests contribute records; stop at the first syntax error
or unfinished request, retaining earlier records. Byte offsets are channel-relative
and half-open. A channel error is exactly `{"kind":"syntax"|"incomplete","offset":R}`,
where R is the start of the first uncommitted request. An empty/fully consumed
channel has error null.

Lines require CRLF, with at most8192 bytes before CRLF. If no LF has arrived and the remaining prefix has at most8193 bytes,
it is incomplete; line content is checked only when LF arrives. A bare LF or an LF beyond the line limit is syntax. A prefix
longer than8193 bytes without LF is syntax. A request line is exactly
`METHOD SP TARGET SP HTTP/1.1 CRLF`; METHOD is a nonempty token and TARGET is
nonempty ASCII visible bytes excluding SP. No alternate whitespace separator.

Header lines are `NAME:value CRLF`, followed by an empty line. NAME is an ASCII
token, case-insensitive for framing rules. Values allow SP..tilde and HTAB only;
strip outer SP/HTAB, preserve all interior bytes. No folding. Initial block size,
including request line and final empty line,is at most65536 bytes and128 fields.
Block size/count checks occur after each complete line; an unterminated line
is governed by the line-prefix rule above.

No Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding means zero body, regardless of method.
Every Content-Length occurrence contains a nonempty comma-separated list of decimal
unsigned values; trim SP/HTAB per member,permit leading zeros,and require all values
identical and <=2^63-1. A Transfer-Encoding is permitted only as one field with
trimmed case-insensitive value `chunked` and no Content-Length. Conflicts are syntax.
A length body is exactly the declared opaque bytes; bytes resembling requests do
not create new messages. Insufficient bytes mean incomplete.

Chunked bodies have hexadecimal unsigned size lines with optional `;` and an
uninterpreted suffix of SP..tilde/HTAB. No whitespace in the size,at least one hex
digit,leading zeros allowed,numeric value <=2^63-1. A nonzero chunk has exactly its
size in opaque bytes and then CRLF. A zero size is followed directly by a trailer
field block and final empty line. Trailer block size (excluding zero-size line)
is at most65536 bytes and128 fields; Host,Content-Length,Transfer-Encoding names
are forbidden there. Other duplicates are preserved. A missing body/suffix/trailer
is incomplete. A wrong complete suffix/line/field is syntax. Concatenate only
nonzero chunk DATA for the body fingerprint. Headers/trailers use the same field
rules. The parser's stated limits are this capture-reader policy,not a full HTTP
implementation or a claim that every tolerated request is RFC-conformant.

## Origin records and paired evidence flags

A channel record has exactly `name`, `bytes`, `requests`, `committed`, `error`.
bytes fingerprints the complete concatenated capture. committed contains the count
of complete published requests after each input part,including zero-length parts.
Requests follow byte order. A request record has exactly `start`, `end`, `method`,
`target`, `host`, `host_count`, `headers`, `body`, `trailers`, `framing`, `owner`,
`owners`, `flags`. Method/target are byte fingerprints. If exactly one Host exists,
host fingerprints its trimmed ASCII-lowercased value; otherwise it is empty.
headers/trailers fingerprint their field blocks encoded as8-byte pair count then
8-byte name length,name bytes,8-byte trimmed value length,value bytes per pair,
preserving name spelling and pair order. framing is `none`, `length`, or `chunked`.
body fingerprints the deframed opaque body.

owner is the provenance label of the request's first byte. owners is an array of
[label,positive byte count] for the complete raw request span,merging equal labels
and ordered by their first occurrence. Raw span includes framing,headers,trailers.
Request flags are a lexicographically sorted set:

- `unattributed`: owner is null.
- `mixed_owner`: some positive byte of the raw request has a different owner.
- `missing_host`/`multiple_host`: zero/more than one Host field (even identical).
- `identity`: a named owner has any mismatch against its expect: method/target
  compare exact bytes,Host must be unique and compares after ASCII case folding.
- `extra`: this is a named owner's second or later request in channel-array order,
  then byte order within each channel.
- `unsent`: named owner emitted no headers/data action,even if datagrams were sent.

origin_count per case counts requests whose first byte has that owner. Case flags
are sorted unique: `missing_origin` if request_frames>0 and count0; `extra_origin`
if count>1; `unsent_origin` if count>0 and request_frames0; `identity` if any owned
request has that flag; `mixed_origin` if any owned request has mixed_owner. These
flags never infer byte equality from checksums and do not label missing client
responses or legitimate origin expansion as vulnerabilities.

See RUNTIME.md for the complete public development and scored execution profiles.

## Local development wrapper (evidence infrastructure)


Local development uses a separate nonroot, chrooted outer process to run the
actual public checker or an opaque installation wrapper. Its limits are 120 s
wall time; 120/121 s soft/hard CPU per process; 2 GiB address space per process;
8 MiB stack; 128 file descriptors; process-count rlimit 64 per UID; 64 MiB per
file; and zero core dumps. The outer stdout/stderr caps are 16 MiB/1 MiB.
It uses the same published scratch path, reset, 0.25 s sampling, 1 GiB/50,000-entry
emergency policy, accounting limitations, and infrastructure-error/no-score
outcome described above. Network access is denied and CPU affinity is unchanged.

Ordinary process creation and same-UID child signaling are allowed in this outer
profile so the checker and opaque installer can launch, stop, and reap children.
Namespace creation remains forbidden: namespace clone flags are rejected,
unshare/setns are denied, and clone3 returns ENOSYS. These outer limits concern
local development evidence infrastructure and impose no candidate algorithm
requirement. Each scored translation invocation, including the public checker's
bounded translation child, continues to use the scored limits above and their
child/thread/signaling denials. The outer profile changes no input semantics,
output schema, serialization, scoring behavior, or submission interface.

## Runtime, resources, and files

Submit the complete project directory at `/workspace/project`, with `main.py` as
its CLI entry. Additional regular source/data files are allowed: the original tree
must have at most256 entries and8MiB total regular-file bytes. Count files and
subdirectories below the project root; exclude the root itself. No symbolic/hard links or special
files. Generated bytecode/cache files are ordinary extra entries and are allowed
within the same budgets. The verifier receives this project tree, not changes to
check.py or files outside it. The project may be reorganized freely and may use
CPython3.11.14 standard library and the provisioned Pydantic2.12.5 dependency set.
Run `cd /workspace/project && python3 -B main.py` with one JSON object on stdin.
The child working directory is the submitted project.
Runtime and restored project are read-only during verification; `/workspace/tmp`
is scratch. The public image installs all dependencies from its included pinned
wheels with no runtime downloads. Local no-Docker staging exposes the same packages
at `/opt/h3deps`; main.py contains the matching path bootstrap.
The public sanity checker runs in the current public workspace as the same image
user; it does not chroot its child, freeze source permissions, or attest the
original submission tree. The private local controller supplies those filesystem
protections for acceptance trials. The public checker needs only public workspace
files and runs a real child
with pipe stdin/stdout. Text I/O, `.buffer`, raw fd 0/1, `fileno`, and `fdopen` work.
An explicit `os._exit(0)` succeeds only if correct JSON bytes reached the pipe.
The checker refuses to launch candidates as root. The image's default user is
UID 1000. Local authoring trials additionally use a nonprivileged chroot worker.

### Scored translation process

Each candidate invocation processes one whole maximum batch. Wall limit is 60 s;
CPU soft/hard limits 20/21 s; address space 512 MiB; stack 8 MiB; 32 FDs; per-file logical size
64 MiB; core dumps disabled; process-count rlimit 64 per UID, with creation of
children and threads denied independently. No CPU affinity binding is applied.
Stdout cap is 16 MiB, stderr cap 1 MiB. Scratch is `/workspace/tmp`, cleared before
each invocation. At 0.25 s intervals the controller checks reachable scratch
files, summing max(logical size, allocated bytes), and directory entries: over
1 GiB or 50,000 entries triggers an infrastructure error without a score. This is
an emergency brake, not an exact storage quota; open-unlinked files and transient
usage are not fully accounted. No additional aggregate scratch quota is used for
local acceptance. There is no aggregate cgroup memory/CPU guarantee in local runs.

Linux x86-64 seccomp returns EPERM for the following syscalls: socket, socketpair,

msgrcv, msgctl, kill, tkill, tgkill, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev,

import ctypes

import resource

DENIED = [41,53,42,29,30,31,64,65,66,220,68,69,70,71,62,200,234,101,

    _fields_ = [('code', ctypes.c_ushort), ('jt', ctypes.c_ubyte),
                ('jf', ctypes.c_ubyte), ('k', ctypes.c_uint)]

"""Frame conversion and deterministic offline client replay.

The replay is a priority-queue state machine.  It deliberately separates the
offline clock from the transport: no real waiting or sockets are involved.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import heapq

from modules.byte_program import concat_many, fingerprint, literal, size


MAX = (1 << 63) - 1


def encoded_action(at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    """Encode one sent/accepted action exactly as the audit receipt format."""
    if type(at) is not int or not 0 <= at <= MAX:
        raise ValueError("action time")
    if type(stream) is not int or not 0 <= stream <= (1 << 32) - 1:
        raise ValueError("action stream")
    if kind not in ("H", "D", "G", "h", "d"):
        raise ValueError("action kind")

    pieces = [literal(at.to_bytes(8, "big") + stream.to_bytes(4, "big") +
                      kind.encode("ascii"))]
    if kind in ("H", "h"):
        pairs = list(data)
        pieces.append(literal(len(pairs).to_bytes(8, "big")))
        for name, value in pairs:
            pieces.append(literal(size(name).to_bytes(8, "big")))
            pieces.append(name)
            pieces.append(literal(size(value).to_bytes(8, "big")))
            pieces.append(value)
    else:
        pieces.append(literal(size(data).to_bytes(8, "big")))
        pieces.append(data)
    pieces.append(literal(bytes((1 if end else 0,))))
    return concat_many(pieces)


class _CaseRuntime:
    __slots__ = (
        "index", "stream", "frames", "frame_index", "state", "at",
        "terminal", "ended", "send_finished", "response_ended",
        "sent_actions", "received_actions", "body_nodes", "body_length",
        "frames_count", "request_frames", "payload_bytes", "response_frames",
    )

    def __init__(self, index, frames):
        self.index = index
        self.stream = 4 * index
        self.frames = frames
        self.frame_index = 0
        self.state = None
        self.at = None
        self.terminal = False
        self.ended = False
        self.send_finished = False
        self.response_ended = False
        self.sent_actions = []
        self.received_actions = []
        self.body_nodes = []
        self.body_length = 0
        self.frames_count = 0
        self.request_frames = 0
        self.payload_bytes = 0
        self.response_frames = 0


class FuzzExecutor:
    """Offline replay engine for the compiled case frames and event tape."""

    def __init__(self, target_ip=None, target_port=None, domain=None):
        self.target_ip = target_ip
        self.target_port = target_port
        self.domain = domain

    @staticmethod
    def _convert_single_case_frames(frames):
        # Compiled frames already carry byte-program values.  Keeping this
        # adapter makes the conversion boundary explicit for callers.
        return list(frames)

    def send_payload(self, cases, events, timeout_ms):
        if type(timeout_ms) is not int or not 0 <= timeout_ms <= MAX:
            raise ValueError("timeout")
        runtimes = [_CaseRuntime(i, self._convert_single_case_frames(c.frames))
                    for i, c in enumerate(cases)]
        by_stream = {rt.stream: rt for rt in runtimes}

        # Heap keys: (virtual time, phase, stable order, sequence, action, data)
        # phase -1 initial starts, 0 external events, 1 pause completions,
        # phase 2 timeouts.  This encodes the protocol's tie ordering.
        queue = []
        sequence = 0

        def push(time, phase, order, action, payload=None):
            nonlocal sequence
            heapq.heappush(queue, (time, phase, order, sequence, action, payload))
            sequence += 1

        for index in range(len(runtimes)):
            push(0, -1, index, "start")

        for index, event in enumerate(events):
            push(event.at, 0, index, "external", event)

        def terminate(rt, state, at):
            if not rt.terminal:
                rt.terminal = True
                rt.state = state
                rt.at = at

        def add_payload(rt, amount):
            total = rt.payload_bytes + amount
            if total > MAX:
                raise ValueError("payload byte budget")
            rt.payload_bytes = total

        def emit(rt, kind, value, end):
            action = encoded_action(0, rt.stream, kind, value, end)
            # Patch the time portion without reconstructing the action: the
            # action was encoded at a placeholder time, so rebuild at the
            # actual current virtual time instead.
            raise AssertionError("emit placeholder must not be called")

        def run_frames(rt, now):
            while rt.frame_index < len(rt.frames):
                if rt.terminal:
                    return
                frame = rt.frames[rt.frame_index]
                kind = frame.kind

                if kind == "sleep":
                    rt.frame_index += 1
                    wake = now + frame.time
                    if wake > MAX:
                        raise ValueError("virtual time budget")
                    push(wake, 1, rt.index, "wake")
                    return

                # A sleep does not finish the request send side, but every
                # other frame after End_Stream is a send error and is not
                # emitted.
                if rt.ended:
                    terminate(rt, "send_error", now)
                    return

                if kind == "headers":
                    pairs = frame.value
                    action = encoded_action(now, rt.stream, "H", pairs,
                                            frame.end)
                    rt.sent_actions.append(action)
                    rt.frames_count += 1
                    rt.request_frames += 1
                    add_payload(rt, sum(size(n) + size(v) for n, v in pairs))
                    if frame.end:
                        rt.ended = True
                elif kind == "data":
                    value = frame.value
                    action = encoded_action(now, rt.stream, "D", value,
                                            frame.end)
                    rt.sent_actions.append(action)
                    rt.frames_count += 1
                    rt.request_frames += 1
                    add_payload(rt, value.size)
                    if frame.end:
                        rt.ended = True
                elif kind == "datagram":
                    value = frame.value
                    action = encoded_action(now, rt.stream, "G", value, False)
                    rt.sent_actions.append(action)
                    rt.frames_count += 1
                    add_payload(rt, value.size)
                    # Datagrams never close the request send side.
                else:  # pragma: no cover - schema rejects other kinds
                    raise ValueError("frame kind")

                rt.frame_index += 1

            # The frame sequence is exhausted: this is send-finish.
            rt.send_finished = True
            if rt.response_ended:
                terminate(rt, "ok", now)
            else:
                deadline = now + timeout_ms
                if deadline > MAX:
                    raise ValueError("virtual time budget")
                push(deadline, 2, rt.index, "timeout")

        def accept_response(rt, event, now):
            if rt.terminal or rt.response_ended:
                return
            if event.kind == "headers":
                action = encoded_action(now, rt.stream, "h", event.fields,
                                        event.end)
                rt.received_actions.append(action)
            else:
                value = event.data
                action = encoded_action(now, rt.stream, "d", value,
                                        event.end)
                rt.received_actions.append(action)
                total = rt.body_length + value.size
                if total > MAX:
                    raise ValueError("response body budget")
                rt.body_length = total
                rt.body_nodes.append(value)
            rt.response_frames += 1
            if event.end:
                rt.response_ended = True
                if rt.send_finished:
                    terminate(rt, "ok", now)

        while queue:
            now, phase, order, _, action, payload = heapq.heappop(queue)

            if action == "start":
                rt = runtimes[order]
                if not rt.terminal:
                    run_frames(rt, now)
                continue

            if action == "external":
                event = payload
                if event.kind == "close":
                    for rt in runtimes:
                        terminate(rt, "closed", now)
                else:
                    rt = by_stream.get(event.stream)
                    if rt is not None:
                        accept_response(rt, event, now)
                continue

            if action == "wake":
                rt = runtimes[order]
                if not rt.terminal:
                    run_frames(rt, now)
                continue

            if action == "timeout":
                rt = runtimes[order]
                if (not rt.terminal and rt.send_finished and
                        not rt.response_ended):
                    terminate(rt, "timeout", now)
                continue

        output = []
        for rt in runtimes:
            if not rt.terminal:
                raise ValueError("unterminated case")
            sent = concat_many(rt.sent_actions)
            received = concat_many(rt.received_actions)
            body = concat_many(rt.body_nodes)
            output.append({
                "name": cases[rt.index].name,
                "stream": rt.stream,
                "state": rt.state,
                "at": rt.at,
                "frames": rt.frames_count,
                "request_frames": rt.request_frames,
                "payload_bytes": rt.payload_bytes,
                "sent": fingerprint(sent),
                "received": fingerprint(received),
                "response_frames": rt.response_frames,
                "response_body": fingerprint(body),
                "origin_count": 0,
                "flags": [],
            })
        return output

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primitive validation


def exact(obj, keys):
    if type(obj) is not dict or set(obj) != set(keys):
        raise ValueError("object keys")


def exact_allowed(obj, required, allowed):
    if type(obj) is not dict:
        raise ValueError("object type")
    if not required <= set(obj) or not set(obj) <= allowed:
        raise ValueError("object keys")


def integer(value, minimum=0, maximum=MAX):
    if type(value) is not int or not minimum <= value <= maximum:
        raise ValueError("integer")
    return value


def boolean(value):
    if type(value) is not bool:
        raise ValueError("boolean")
    return value


def sequence(value, maximum):
    if type(value) is not list or len(value) > maximum:
        raise ValueError("array")
    return value


def text(value, maximum=65536):
    if type(value) is not str or len(value) > maximum:
        raise ValueError("string")
    try:
        value.encode("utf8")
    except UnicodeEncodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError("string encoding") from exc
    return value


def _ascii(value, maximum=8192):
    text(value, 65536)
    try:
        encoded = value.encode("ascii")
    except UnicodeEncodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError("ascii") from exc
    if len(encoded) > maximum:
        raise ValueError("ascii length")
    return encoded


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation


def _compile_headers(context, frame, case_index, frame_index, fields_count):
    has_mapping = "headers_kv" in frame
    has_pairs = "data_to_transfered" in frame
    if has_mapping == has_pairs:
        raise ValueError("exactly one header representation")
    end = frame.get("End_Stream", False)
    boolean(end)

    pairs = []
    if has_mapping:
        exact_allowed(frame, {"Type", "headers_kv"},
                      {"Type", "headers_kv", "End_Stream"})
        mapping = frame["headers_kv"]
        if type(mapping) is not dict:
            raise ValueError("header mapping")
        if len(mapping) > 128:
            raise ValueError("header block size")
        for pair_index, (name_source, value_source) in enumerate(mapping.items()):
            text(name_source, 65536)
            text(value_source, 65536)
            name = context.template(
                name_source,
                f"case/{case_index}/frame/{frame_index}/h/{pair_index}/n")
            value = context.template(
                value_source,
                f"case/{case_index}/frame/{frame_index}/h/{pair_index}/v")
            pairs.append((name, value))
        fields_count += len(mapping)
    else:
        exact_allowed(frame, {"Type", "data_to_transfered"},
                      {"Type", "data_to_transfered", "End_Stream"})
        raw_pairs = sequence(frame["data_to_transfered"], 128)
        for pair_index, pair in enumerate(raw_pairs):
            sequence(pair, 2)
            if len(pair) != 2:
                raise ValueError("header pair")
            name_source, value_source = pair
            text(name_source, 65536)
            text(value_source, 65536)
            name = context.template(
                name_source,
                f"case/{case_index}/frame/{frame_index}/h/{pair_index}/n")
            value = context.template(
                value_source,
                f"case/{case_index}/frame/{frame_index}/h/{pair_index}/v")
            pairs.append((name, value))
        fields_count += len(raw_pairs)

    return FrameSpec("headers", pairs, end, 0), fields_count


def _compile_frame(context, frame, case_index, frame_index, fields_count,
                   pause_sum):
    if type(frame) is not dict:
        raise ValueError("frame")
    kind = frame.get("Type")
    if kind not in ("headers", "data", "datagram", "sleep"):
        raise ValueError("frame type")

    if kind == "sleep":
        exact(frame, {"Type", "Time_to_Stop"})
        duration = integer(frame["Time_to_Stop"], 0, MAX)
        pause_sum += duration
        if pause_sum > MAX:
            raise ValueError("pause budget")
        return FrameSpec("sleep", None, False, duration), fields_count, pause_sum

    if kind == "headers":
        compiled, fields_count = _compile_headers(
            context, frame, case_index, frame_index, fields_count)
        return compiled, fields_count, pause_sum

    exact_allowed(frame, {"Type", "data_to_transfered"},
                  {"Type", "data_to_transfered", "End_Stream"})
    end = frame.get("End_Stream", True)
    boolean(end)
    source = text(frame["data_to_transfered"], 65536)
    data = context.template(
        source, f"case/{case_index}/frame/{frame_index}/data")
    return FrameSpec(kind, data, end, 0), fields_count, pause_sum


def compile_cases(cases, context):
    """Compile an already root-validated case array into typed case specs."""
    names = set()
    compiled_cases = []
    field_pairs = 0
    frame_budget = 0
    timeout_placeholder = MAX
    for case_index, case in enumerate(cases):
        exact(case, {"name", "frames", "expect"})
        name = text(case["name"], 32)
        if NAME_RE.fullmatch(name) is None or name in names:
            raise ValueError("case name")
        names.add(name)

        raw_frames = sequence(case["frames"], 50000)
        frame_budget += len(raw_frames)
        pause_sum = 0
        frames = []
        for frame_index, raw_frame in enumerate(raw_frames):
            frame, field_pairs, pause_sum = _compile_frame(
                context, raw_frame, case_index, frame_index, field_pairs,
                pause_sum)
            frames.append(frame)

        expect = case["expect"]
        exact(expect, {"method", "target", "host"})
        expected = {}
        for key in ("method", "target", "host"):
            encoded = _ascii(expect[key], 8192)
            if not encoded or any(value < 33 or value > 126 for value in encoded):
                raise ValueError("expected identity")
            expected[key] = encoded
        if TOKEN_BYTES_RE.fullmatch(expected["method"]) is None:
            raise ValueError("expected method")

        # The caller replaces this conservative value with the real timeout
        # when checking the final sum.
        compiled_cases.append(CaseSpec(
            name=name, frames=frames, method=expected["method"],
            target=expected["target"], host=expected["host"]))
    return compiled_cases, frame_budget, field_pairs


def compile_document(document):
    """Validate the complete JSON document and compile all templates."""
    exact(document, {"seed", "definitions", "timeout_ms", "cases", "events",
                     "channels"})

    seed = text(document["seed"], 64)
    if SEED_RE.fullmatch(seed) is None:
        raise ValueError("seed")

    raw_definitions = sequence(document["definitions"], 8192)
    for row in raw_definitions:
        if type(row) is not list or len(row) != 2:
            raise ValueError("definition pair")
        text(row[0], 32)
        text(row[1], 8192)
    # Context performs the precise identifier, keyword, AST-depth and
    # expression-semantics checks in definition order.
    context = Context(raw_definitions, seed)

    timeout_ms = integer(document["timeout_ms"], 1, 10 ** 9)

    raw_cases = sequence(document["cases"], 2000)
    cases, frame_budget, field_pairs = compile_cases(raw_cases, context)
    if frame_budget > 50000:
        raise ValueError("combined budget")

    # Validate the per-case pause + timeout budgets after compilation.
    for raw_case, case in zip(raw_cases, cases):
        pause_sum = sum(frame.time for frame in case.frames
                        if frame.kind == "sleep")
        if pause_sum + timeout_ms > MAX:
            raise ValueError("time budget")

    raw_events = sequence(document["events"], 50000)
    if frame_budget + len(raw_events) > 50000:
        raise ValueError("combined budget")
    events = []
    for event_index, record in enumerate(raw_events):
        if type(record) is not dict:
            raise ValueError("event")
        kind = record.get("kind")
        if kind not in ("close", "headers", "data"):
            raise ValueError("event kind")

        if kind == "close":
            exact(record, {"at", "kind"})
            at = integer(record["at"], 0, MAX)
            events.append(EventSpec(at=at, kind="close"))
            continue

        exact(record, {"at", "kind", "stream", "end",
                       "fields" if kind == "headers" else "data"})
        at = integer(record["at"], 0, MAX)
        stream = integer(record["stream"], 0, (1 << 32) - 1)
        end = boolean(record["end"])

        if kind == "headers":
            raw_fields = sequence(record["fields"], 128)
            fields = []
            for pair_index, pair in enumerate(raw_fields):
                sequence(pair, 2)
                if len(pair) != 2:
                    raise ValueError("event field pair")
                name_source, value_source = pair
                text(name_source, 65536)
                text(value_source, 65536)
                name = context.template(
                    name_source,
                    f"event/{event_index}/h/{pair_index}/n")
                value = context.template(
                    value_source,
                    f"event/{event_index}/h/{pair_index}/v")
                fields.append((name, value))
            field_pairs += len(raw_fields)
            events.append(EventSpec(at=at, kind="headers", stream=stream,
                                    fields=fields, end=end))
        else:
            source = text(record["data"], 65536)
            data = context.template(source, f"event/{event_index}/data")
            events.append(EventSpec(at=at, kind="data", stream=stream,
                                    data=data, end=end))

    raw_channels = sequence(document["channels"], 256)
    channels = []
    channel_names = set()
    part_budget = 0
    for channel_index, channel in enumerate(raw_channels):
        exact(channel, {"name", "parts"})
        name = text(channel["name"], 32)
        if NAME_RE.fullmatch(name) is None or name in channel_names:
            raise ValueError("channel name")
        channel_names.add(name)

        raw_parts = sequence(channel["parts"], 50000)
        part_budget += len(raw_parts)
        parts = []
        total_length = 0
        for part_index, part in enumerate(raw_parts):
            exact(part, {"case", "data"})
            owner = part["case"]
            if owner is not None:
                if type(owner) is not str or owner not in {c.name for c in cases}:
                    raise ValueError("owner label")
            source = text(part["data"], 65536)
            data = context.template(
                source, f"channel/{channel_index}/part/{part_index}/data")
            total_length += size(data)
            if total_length > MAX:
                raise ValueError("channel length")
            parts.append(PartSpec(owner=owner, data=data))
        channels.append(ChannelSpec(name=name, parts=parts))

    if frame_budget + len(raw_events) + part_budget > 50000:
        raise ValueError("combined budget")
    if field_pairs > 32768:
        raise ValueError("combined header budget")

    return DocumentSpec(seed=seed, timeout_ms=timeout_ms, cases=cases,
                        events=events, channels=channels, contexts=context)

"""Offline payload compilation, client replay and origin evidence audit."""
import gc
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import sys

# The local no-Docker worker stages the pinned wheels here.  The public image
# also has them installed normally; this path is harmless when absent.
if Path('/opt/h3deps').is_dir():
    sys.path.insert(0, '/opt/h3deps')

from schema import compile_document
from modules.fuzz_adapter import FuzzExecutor
from modules.capture_audit import audit_channels


MAX_RAW = 8 * 1024 ** 2


def pairs(items):
    out = {}
    for key, value in items:
        if key in out:
            raise ValueError('duplicate key')
        out[key] = value
    return out


def bad_constant(value):
    raise ValueError('nonfinite JSON')


def finite_float(value):
    result = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError('nonfinite JSON')
    return result


def run(document):
    spec = compile_document(document)
    sent = FuzzExecutor().send_payload(spec.cases, spec.events,
                                       spec.timeout_ms)
    origin = audit_channels(spec.channels, spec.cases, sent)
    return {'cases': sent, 'channels': origin}


def main():
    gc.disable()
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read(MAX_RAW + 1)
        if len(raw) > MAX_RAW:

        document = json.loads(

            object_pairs_hook=pairs,
            parse_constant=bad_constant,
            parse_float=finite_float,
        )

    except Exception:
        result = {'error': 'input'}

    encoded = json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(',', ':'),
                         allow_nan=False).encode('ascii')
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(encoded + b'\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

1 # Offline regression evidence pipeline, contract 3.0
   2 
   3 Repair and extend the provided H3Act project so `python3 main.py` compiles payloads,
   4 replays decoded client events, and audits compressed origin captures. The existing
   5 schema models, FuzzExecutor adapter, and HttpClient form the application, not an
   6 external service. The offline clock is a socket-free coroutine utility. Complete
   7 the byte-program and audit extension and repair integration/lifecycle defects.
   8 Equivalent implementations are accepted; internal algorithms are your choice.
   9 
  10 This model starts after transport delivery/field decoding. It sends no packets,
  11 runs no model, and has no live CDN, QPACK, TLS, SSH, GPU, response cache, or wall-time
  12 simulation. Its receipt encoding below is an audit format, not HTTP/3 wire format.
  13 Diagnostic flags describe this paired recording, not a proof of a real exploit.
  14 
  15 ## Input and domain
  16 
  17 Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object without a byte-order mark, with surrounding
  18 JSON whitespace allowed.
  19 Reject duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8/JSON, nonfinite numbers (including overflowing
  20 exponents), trailing values, wrong types, unknown/missing keys, or budget violations
  21 with exactly `{"error":"input"}` and exit0. Every input string must encode as
  22 UTF-8; lone Unicode surrogates are invalid. Booleans are not integers. No coercion.
  23 Validate the whole input, including frames/events that ultimately are not used.
  24 Otherwise output the result described below and exit0. Emit JSON only on stdout.
  25 
  26 The root has exactly `seed`, `definitions`, `timeout_ms`, `cases`, `events`, `channels`.
  27 `seed` is 0-64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen. `timeout_ms` is an integer
  28 in [1,1000000000]. Names of cases/channels are unique within their kind and use
  29 1-32 of those ASCII characters. Arrays preserve order. Object member order is
  30 irrelevant except for the ordered header mapping described below.
  31 
  32 Budgets are inclusive: raw stdin8MiB; definitions8192; cases2000; channels256;
  33 combined number of case frames + external events + capture parts50000; combined
  34 header pairs in input frames and external events32768; pairs per header block128;
  35 expression source8192 Unicode code points; other template source65536 code points.
  36 Logical byte sequence lengths, channel lengths, receipt lengths, body lengths,
  37 and virtual times are in [0,2^63-1]. Every case's sum of pauses + timeout_ms must
  38 fit this range. At most20000 complete origin requests and40000 complete chunk-size
  39 lines (including zero chunks and lines in an unfinished request) may be examined
  40 across all channels. Count a line in chunk-size position after its CRLF/line-limit
  41 check and before checking the hexadecimal size or suffix; a malformed line
  42 terminator or unfinished line is not counted. These are input-domain budgets, not a scoring objective.
  43 
  44 Compressed captures cover very large objects and repeated boundary probes without
  45 storing their expanded contents. Metadata counts model a batch audit between
  46 experiment rounds; signed64-bit offsets permit sparse capture ranges. Resource
  47 limits support an interactive batch audit and are not a speed ranking. Materialized
  48 traffic volume or the number of discovered diagnostic flags is not a score.
  49 
  50 ## Byte expressions, templates and fingerprints
  51 
  52 `definitions` is an ordered array of `[name, expression]`. Names are distinct,
  53 non-keyword Python identifiers matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}`. An expression
  54 can refer only to earlier definitions. The accepted Python expression syntax is:
  55 Unicode string or bytes literals; nonnegative integer literals <=2^63-1; earlier names; parentheses;
  56 concatenation `+` of byte sequences; repetition `*` with one byte sequence and one
  57 integer (either order); and a byte slice `[lo:hi]` with either endpoint optionally
  58 omitted. A final expression must be bytes, never an integer. Slice endpoints are
  59 integer literals, with 0<=lo<=hi<=length; omitted endpoints mean0/length. No negative
  60 index, nonempty slice step, integer arithmetic, boolean, call, attribute,
  61 list, format string or other syntax is supported. AST nesting depth is at most128,
  62 counting the root expression body as depth0 and every AST child edge, including
  63 slice/operator/context nodes. Parentheses do not add AST depth.
  64 Definition sources use CPython3.11 `ast.parse(source, mode="eval")` as supplied,
  65 without whitespace normalization; sources it rejects are invalid. Empty third
  66 slice components (`[lo:hi:]` or `[::]`) are equivalent to an omitted step.
  67 Unicode string literals encode to UTF-8; bytes literals supply their exact bytes
  68 before any byte operation; slices are byte offsets,
  69 even within an encoded character. An empty sequence and zero repetitions are legal.
  70 
  71 Every template is a JSON string. A string starting `{{` and ending `}}` is a whole
  72 expression template: strip those outer markers and surrounding expression whitespace,
  73 then evaluate it. Other strings are UTF-8 literal data, except each occurrence of
  74 `<<random_string>>` is replaced by the first20 lowercase hex characters of SHA256
  75 of the UTF-8 string `seed/coordinate/occurrence`. Occurrences are numbered from0
  76 left to right independently per template. Tokens inside expression string literals
  77 are literal data. Markers embedded in an ordinary literal are not expressions.
  78 Coordinates are exactly:

  82 - External event i: `event/i/data`, or `event/i/h/k/n` and `/v` for headers.
  83 - Capture part j of channel i: `channel/i/part/j/data`.

  86 `{"n":N,"h":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}`: N is byte length and h is the 16-digit lowercase
  87 hex value of sum((b[i]+1)*257^(N-1-i)) modulo2^64. Empty bytes have n0 and all-zero h.
  88 A fingerprint is a requested exact checksum; checksum equality is not asserted
  89 to prove byte equality. Routing-identity comparisons below compare actual bytes.

  92 
  93 Each case is exactly `{"name":NAME,"frames":[FRAME,...],"expect":EXPECT}`.

 119 - `{"at":T,"kind":"headers","stream":S,"fields":[[name,value],...],"end":BOOL}`

 121 - `{"at":T,"kind":"close"}`

 124 event fields/data as templates. The event array may be out of timestamp order.
 125 At equal time, ordering is: all initial case starts first; external events in

 133 paused must be retained. A case is `ok` when both its frame sequence is exhausted

 136 close terminates every nonterminal case as `closed`, including paused senders,

 143 ## Client receipts and output case records

 155 Case records follow input case order and have exactly:
 156 `name`, `stream`, `state`, `at`, `frames`, `request_frames`, `payload_bytes`, `sent`,

def _parse_request(cap: Capture, start: int, state: _AuditState):
    content, cursor = _line(cap, start)
    method, target = _request_line(content)
    block_start = start
    if cursor - block_start > 65536:
        raise _ParseFailure("syntax")

    headers, cursor = _header_block_fast(cap, block_start, cursor)

    framing, body_length = _framing(headers)
    body_fp = (0, 0)
    trailers_fp = _fields_fingerprint([])

    if framing == "none":
        end = cursor
    elif framing == "length":
        body_start = cursor
        if cap.total - body_start < body_length:
            raise _ParseFailure("incomplete")
        end = body_start + body_length
        body_fp = cap.fp_range(body_start, end)
    else:  # chunked
        body_total = 0
        end = cursor
        trailers = []
        while True:
            content, next_cursor = _line(cap, cursor)
            # The budget counts a line only after its CRLF and line-limit
            # checks, and before inspecting the hexadecimal size or suffix.
            state.chunk_lines += 1
            if state.chunk_lines > 40000:
                raise ValueError("chunk line budget")
            chunk_length = _chunk_size(content)
            cursor = next_cursor

            if chunk_length == 0:
                trailer_start = cursor
                while True:
                    content, next_cursor = _line(cap, cursor)
                    if next_cursor - trailer_start > 65536:
                        raise _ParseFailure("syntax")
                    if content == b"":
                        cursor = next_cursor
                        break
                    if len(trailers) + 1 > 128:
                        raise _ParseFailure("syntax")
                    field = _field(content)
                    if field[0].lower() in _FORBIDDEN_TRAILER_NAMES:
                        raise _ParseFailure("syntax")
                    trailers.append(field)
                    cursor = next_cursor
                trailers_fp = _fields_fingerprint(trailers)
                end = cursor
                break

            if body_total + chunk_length > MAX:
                raise ValueError("body length budget")
            data_start = cursor
            if cap.total - data_start < chunk_length:
                raise _ParseFailure("incomplete")
            data_end = data_start + chunk_length
            if cap.total - data_end < 2:
                raise _ParseFailure("incomplete")
            if cap.read(data_end, data_end + 2) != b"\r\n":
                raise _ParseFailure("syntax")
            body_fp = _combine_fp(body_fp, cap.fp_range(data_start, data_end))

            cursor = data_end + 2

    host_values = [value for name, value in headers
